# 0.3.1

Common Measure rules on which content an AI agent may take in, records where
each piece came from and what it cost, and measures whether it helped. This
release adds three hosts to the ones the binary registers itself with, tells
the programs behind one registration apart in the record, lets a managed
machine join a hub with one command, and changes what strict policy does
with personal data found on a public page. The source stays available under
the Functional Source License, FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0; the protocol contracts and
evidence format specifications under `docs/contracts/` are CC-BY-4.0.

## What the release holds

- `commonmeasure-linux-x64`, `commonmeasure-linux-arm64`,
  `commonmeasure-darwin-arm64`, `commonmeasure-darwin-x64` and
  `commonmeasure-win-x64.exe`: one prebuilt `commonmeasure` binary per
  supported platform, named as the plugin's launcher names them.
- `commonmeasure-plugin-0.3.1.tar.gz`: the Claude Code plugin as its own
  marketplace, bundling all five binaries.
- `install.sh`: the installer.
- `SHA256SUMS`: the SHA-256 of every other asset.

## Installing

The installer needs `curl` and `sha256sum` or `shasum`, and no account:

```sh
curl -fsSL -o install.sh https://github.com/commonmeasure/commonmeasure/releases/download/v0.3.1/install.sh
sh install.sh --tag v0.3.1
```

It downloads this platform's binary with the checksum list, verifies the
checksum before the binary is placed in `~/.local/bin`, and checks that the
installed binary reports this version. `--plugin DIR` also unpacks the
plugin archive into `DIR` and prints the two commands that install it into
Claude Code. A binary installed by the previous release is replaced in place
by running the same command again.

To register the installed binary with a host directly:

```sh
commonmeasure install claude          # or codex, pi, claude-desktop, cursor
```

## Hosts

- **Claude Desktop and Cursor** take the same `install`, `uninstall` and
  `doctor` commands as Claude Code, Codex and Pi. `install claude-desktop`
  writes one entry into the application's own configuration file; Claude
  Desktop has no hook surface, so its crossings are mediated or nothing.
  The application starts one server for its chat client and one for its
  local agent mode; each that makes a call leaves its own session naming
  its client. `install cursor` writes the server into `~/.cursor/mcp.json`
  and four hooks into `~/.cursor/hooks.json`, so a Cursor session records
  the nudge, its prompts and turns, and every tool result Cursor's hooks
  carry, a third-party MCP result included, under Cursor's own conversation
  identifier. `uninstall` for either host removes exactly what `install`
  wrote and deletes no file.
- **One Codex registration serves three programs.** `install codex` writes
  `default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"` on the server's table, because
  Codex asks before every MCP call otherwise and its non-interactive runs
  refuse a call that would ask; `doctor codex` reports the mode. The Codex
  CLI, the ChatGPT desktop app and the Codex IDE extension all read that
  table. A session a real Codex CLI run recorded through it is committed
  under `demo/host-sessions/codex/`.
- **The record names the client.** The MCP server records the client's own
  name and version from its `initialize` request, once before the first
  record a tool call leaves (`client_identified`) and on every mediated
  crossing after it (`client`), so the programs behind one registration are
  told apart in the record. A server that is started and never asked for
  anything leaves no session file. `commonmeasure mcp --host` accepts
  `claude-desktop`, `cursor`, `copilot-cli` and `vscode` beside the three
  hosts it registers, and refuses any other word with the list.
- **Hook commands name their host.** Every hook command the Claude Code
  registration writes now carries `--host claude-code`, and a hook told
  that refuses a payload in another host's shape, or any payload when
  Cursor's environment variable is set, recording and printing nothing.
  Cursor and VS Code can load Claude Code's hook file and run its commands
  with payloads of their own; without the refusal those runs would have
  been recorded as Claude Code sessions.
- **The installer's last line** names the host registration first: `Next:
  commonmeasure install claude (or codex, pi) to register with your host,
  then work a session, …`. The previous installer said to work a session,
  which recorded nothing until the host was registered.
- `doctor claude` reports an enabled plugin whose files are in place as the
  registration, and warns about double recording only when a direct
  registration stands beside it.

## Policy

- **Personal data on a public page is recorded, not refused.** Under
  `strict`, a PII finding refuses a crossing only where the source is
  internal or private: a named internal prefix, a loopback or private
  address reached under `allow_private_hosts`, or the operator's own
  corpus. On a public source the finding is recorded on the crossing, with
  its categories and offsets, and the crossing is admitted, because the
  published contact details of a public page are not the personal data the
  detector exists to keep out of a model. The previous release refused
  every finding under `strict`. A new policy switch, `refuse_on_pii: true`,
  restores the refusal on every source.
- **The policy identity schema is now `contextops-policy-identity/v2`.**
  The `refuse_on_pii` value enters the identity, so every policy's digest
  changes with this release, whether or not the policy sets the switch. An
  operator who quoted a `sha256:` policy identity from the previous release
  in a review, a fleet record or a hub comparison will see a different
  digest for the same policy file from this binary. The new digest is not
  drift: it is the same policy under the new schema, and the schema name is
  recorded beside every digest so the two are never compared as equals.
  The pre-image and the recomputation are in
  `docs/contracts/fleet-status.md` §Policy identity.
- **A processor refusal says what happened.** When the PII detector or the
  injection screen refuses, the tool error says the content was fetched and
  did not enter the context, and that its hash is on the record, because
  that is what happened; a host-policy refusal still says the crossing was
  refused before any bytes moved.

## Managed machines and the hub

- **`connect --managed` joins a hub with one command.** It enrols, reads the
  hub's policy-signing key under the ingest key it was given, pins that key
  and the hub's policy address in `deployment.json`, and makes a first
  policy synchronisation, so a managed machine writes no file by hand. The
  pin prefers the absolute policy address the hub gives and accepts only an
  `https` address, or `http` to a loopback origin; a hub whose address
  fails that rule is refused before anything is written. A refused pin or a
  first synchronisation that activated nothing exits non-zero after its
  account, with the enrolment kept. `disconnect` removes a deployment
  pinned to the hub being left and keeps one pinned to another.
- **Policy is refreshed at session start.** A managed edge refreshes its
  policy from the hub when a session starts, through the hook or the MCP
  server's start for a session no hook refreshed, and before a relay
  delivery; each refresh is recorded (`policy_sync`) and the session's
  records name the policy in force. The refresh waits three seconds,
  including name resolution, and a hub that does not answer costs the wait
  and nothing else.
- **An expired envelope is enforced and reported stale.** A managed edge
  keeps enforcing the last envelope it applied after that envelope's
  validity ends, and reports it stale in every record and in fleet status
  until the hub renews it; a renewal that carries the same policy refreshes
  the window.
- **The envelope digest is over the policy as carried.** The edge checks a
  policy envelope's digest over the policy bytes as the envelope carries
  them, before parsing, so a hub need not reproduce the edge's own
  serialisation; the loader's digest is kept beside it for the on-disk
  comparison, and fleet status carries both with whether the file was
  edited since.
- **The refused count leaves with the session.** Every batch the relay
  delivers carries `refused`, the session's running total of crossings
  policy refused, and nothing else about them: no address, no reason. A
  refusal after the session's last admitted crossing is delivered too. The
  hub keeps the highest count it has accepted per session.
- A delivery failure prints the edge key's standing first, so a revoked key
  is named before the failure it caused; a 401 from the policy endpoint is
  recorded as `unauthenticated`.

## Documents

- The walkthrough (`docs/GETTING-STARTED.md`) opens on the installed
  binary and the host registration; nothing before its last section needs
  a checkout or a toolchain.
- A hub page (`docs/HUB.md`) states what the hub is, what leaves a machine
  and what never does, how a machine joins and how policy arrives.
- The worked example is `docs/guide/four-fetches.md`, "Four fetches, two
  refused", with its policy at `demo/policy/four-fetches.json`.
- The host integration contract (`docs/contracts/host-integration.md`)
  covers five hosts, and its verification table separates registration,
  mediated and observed paths per host and grades each.

## Verified on this release

The installer and the plugin archive are exercised on Linux in a container
with no toolchain and no credential, and the macOS Apple Silicon binary is
built and run on the same kind of machine. The Linux arm64, macOS Intel
and Windows binaries are built and checksummed by the same run; the
installer has not been run on Windows.

## Known limitations

The committed demonstration runs under `demo/output` were recorded on a
developer machine and carry that machine's file paths. They are
hash-sealed as recorded and will be regenerated in a later release.
Claude Desktop's and Cursor's registrations are verified by tests that
write and read the hosts' files; no session recorded through either
application is committed yet.
